newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Rwanda insists it not involved in Zaire clashes.
newsitem.headline: Rwanda insists it not involved in Zaire clashes.

text.p: Rwanda insisted on Monday it was not involved in clashes in eastern Zaire and called on Kinshasa not to expel ethnic Tutsis who have always lived in the country and should be considered its nationals.
The Rwandan government, in a statement issued by its embassy in Brussels, urged Rwandan refugees in eastern Zaire not to get involved in violence there and instead return home.

"The government of Rwanda (wants) to inform the Rwandan people and International community it has no part whatsoever in the war and troubles going on between...the armed forces of the Government of Zaire who intend to expel from Zaire the Zairean citizens known as "Banyamulenge", the statement said.

An estimated 300,000 Rwandan and Burundian Hutu refugees are fleeing the conflict in eastern Zaire pitting the ethnic Tutsis, who have lived in Zaire since the 18th century, against the Zairean army, which says Rwanda is helping the Tutsis.
The U.N. fears the conflict could spread with the help of Tutsi-dominated armies in Burundi and Rwanda.

Rwanda said in the statement it was only asking Zaire and the international community that the ethnic Tutsis in Zaire "should not be subject to extermination or be expelled from their own country given that they are Zaireans like any other Zairean citizen, Zaire being their home country".
Ethnic tensions in the volatile region worsened in the wake of the arrival of a million Rwandan Hutu refugees after 1994's genocide of Tutsis.

The U.N. refugee agency UNHCR said between 5,000 and 10,000 Rwandan refugees fled into Rwanda from eastern Zaire on Sunday morning, the first significant return of Rwandan Hutu refugees into Rwanda since the current crisis began.
"Rwandan refugees should run away from (the) troubles and come back home where they can find security," the Rwandan government statement said.
